cards.issue_title: Charge notes use legal jargon instead of friendly-lawyer advice
summary_4_lines: On Explore banks Other charges, the notes under Rate change charge (and they said Overdue and EMI bounce notes are the same) are written in legal terms like MCLR and BPLR.
They said every symbol they have to read uses only legal language.
They want it to sound like a friendly lawyer on the customer’s team: how the rate is decided, and when to pick floating vs fixed.
They do not want the customer to have to use legal language.
cards.pinpoint: On Explore banks Other charges, Rate change charge notes (and they said Overdue and EMI bounce notes are the same) use legal terms such as MCLR and BPLR instead of friendly-lawyer advice on how the rate is decided and when to choose floating vs fixed.
cards.on_screen_object: Other charges Notes, especially details#hlc-charge-note-rate-change-charge (MCLR / BPLR / benchmark-switch text), plus overdue and EMI-bounce notes they called the same
quotes_sample: I feel that all the symbols that I have to read, I have to use only legal language.
Versus it should be like a friendly lawyer who is in your team to help you out.
For example, look at this. MCLR, BPLR, these are the things.
related_discussion_one_liners: Want five or six agencies whose rate is taken (raw ASR HR; likely repo / external-benchmark) with no advantage or disadvantage — the customer chooses.
If not much stress, go with “RBI report” (ASR; notes talk RBI / repo-linked); if market/economy is going down or rates will rise, take fixed.
Fixed can be 0.25 higher than floating (already written); intelligence should say if India is going down do not take fixed — floating is better long term.
Same-note check: overdue and EMI bounce notes are “again the same.”
Thematic cousin (not this file’s continuation): wb-rec-260816-0013 Rate change as too complex/legal; previous folder wb-rec-260816-0029 ended on EMI-miss drawers and labels, not this wording.
cards.distinct_from_other_files_in_this_folder: This is the Other charges notes/symbols using legal jargon (MCLR, BPLR) instead of friendly-lawyer rate-choice advice, not the bank table missing scheme names.

cards.issue_title: Table does not show scheme names or multiple schemes of the same bank
summary_4_lines: On Explore banks, the bank table and the Yes Bank More drawer do not show a real scheme name — only a generic product such as Home Loan.
They said they cannot tell which scheme they are looking at, and the table cannot show two schemes of the same bank.
They walked women vs general schemes and PMAY: a woman can be eligible for more than one scheme at once and must be told.
They also talked about auto-picking the best scheme and hiding the name — that is their debate, not a second issue.
cards.pinpoint: On Explore banks, the table and Yes Bank More drawer do not show a real scheme name, and they cannot show two applicable schemes of the same bank, so a customer who qualifies for more than one (women vs general, PMAY) cannot see or choose.
cards.on_screen_object: Bank options table lender cells (scheme/product line under the bank name) and Yes Bank More drawer (Scheme name: Home Loan); Purpose Regular/Top-up; Filters Women applicant
quotes_sample: I don't even know the name of the scheme.
But where are the multiple schemes?
You can't use any bank of the same bank in this table.
related_discussion_one_liners: Top-up vs Regular: one thought Top-up meant two schemes of the same bank; corrected as a purpose selection, and the table still shows one scheme per bank.
If only one scheme can apply, they do not need the name upfront — “the customer only has to pay the bank off. But there is no scheme.”
Canara Bank (ASR Canada Bank): women get a discount, not different schemes, but the bank wrote the scheme is only for women — they disagreed with that writing.

“What should we do in Himalaya?” (raw ASR): pick the best scheme and hide the name versus the woman must know two schemes should be selected (PM Yojana and SCM Yojana); closing: do not add scheme-name information.
Last-minute wrap-up: compare-and-apply product still not taken; homepage and compare done so far — not a second issue.
